page: Microsoft Azure D192ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, offering 11339 GB of local disk capacity. The x86_64 architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier (top 10%) for multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU score, and extended instruction execution. Memory bandwidth tests show top-tier read and write speeds, reaching 13906.45 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 677.36 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Single-core CPU performance and Passmark memory scores fall within the average range (middle 50%). In database and memory-store operations, the server demonstrates top-tier performance, achieving 250.73 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and high throughput in Passmark database operations. Large-model LLM inference is top-tier for prompt processing but drops to average for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D192ds_v7 provides high resource density by combining massive compute capacity with a substantial 11339 GB local storage allocation, reducing the need for separate high-capacity block storage attachments. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly efficient for workloads that scale horizontally across cores without requiring extreme memory-to-CPU ratios. This server is optimized for large-scale database operations, high-throughput static web serving, multi-threaded data decompression, and CPU-based machine learning prompt processing.
